title: Adult Essential Hypertension Screening and Confirmation

evidenceAudit.scope: Adult screening, standardised measurement, confirmation, initial organ-damage assessment, escalation and follow-up were checked against the opened NHC/SHA 2023 hypertension guideline and the opened Saudi MOH hypertension page.
findings: The Saudi guideline separates thresholds used to diagnose hypertension from thresholds used to consider treatment; this topic does not merge them.
Home and ambulatory measurements supplement office measurement and identify white-coat or masked hypertension.
The source requires a clinical and laboratory evaluation for target-organ damage and secondary causes after suspected hypertension.
unverifiedSections: Local availability and calibration programme for validated blood-pressure devices.
A second current international guideline could not be opened; NICE NG136 returned HTTP 403.
Treatment selection is outside this screening-and-confirmation topic.

pathophysiology.summary: Sustained arterial pressure above the diagnostic threshold causes progressive vascular and target-organ injury. The condition is usually silent, so reliable measurement and confirmation are central to diagnosis.
keyMechanisms: Persistent excess arterial pressure injures blood vessels over time.
Vascular injury and arterial wall change reduce efficient blood flow and contribute to cardiac and cerebrovascular complications.
Ongoing pressure-related injury affects the heart, brain, kidneys and eyes; the initial evaluation looks for damage in these organs.

symptoms: Usually no symptoms, including at markedly elevated readings.
Headache, dizziness, nosebleed, visual change or tinnitus may occur but cannot confirm hypertension.
physicalSigns: Elevated blood pressure measured with a validated device and correct technique.
Possible signs of cardiac, neurological, renal or retinal target-organ damage.
Possible clues to a secondary cause on cardiovascular, renal, endocrine or vascular examination.
redFlags: Blood pressure above 190/120 mmHg with new or worsening hypertension-mediated organ damage: treat as a hypertensive emergency pathway.
Chest pain, dyspnoea, acute neurological deficit, confusion or visual loss with severe elevation: urgent hospital assessment.
Pregnancy with elevated blood pressure: use a pregnancy-specific pathway.
precipitants: Obesity, physical inactivity, high dietary salt intake, smoking and advancing age.
Kidney, endocrine or thyroid disease, sleep apnoea and pregnancy.
Medicines, contraceptive pills, stimulants or recreational drugs that raise blood pressure.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Office blood pressure is elevated while correctly performed home or ambulatory averages are below the applicable diagnostic threshold.
Office blood pressure is below the diagnostic threshold while home or ambulatory readings are elevated.
The reading falls after rest and correct cuff, position and repeat-measurement technique; review pain, acute illness and substances.
History, examination or baseline tests suggest renal, endocrine, vascular, sleep-related, pregnancy-related or medicine-related disease.

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Saudi office, daytime ambulatory or average home diagnostic threshold
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: 130/80 mmHg or higher when measured appropriately.

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Saudi threshold at which treatment is considered
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Above 140/90 mmHg in the office; 130/80 mmHg or higher for 24-hour ambulatory average; 135/85 mmHg or higher for daytime ambulatory or average home readings.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Screen at each healthcare visit when feasible; use annual screening after age 40 or with risk factors, and every 3-5 years for other adults.
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Average of three measurements meets or exceeds 130/80 mmHg after correct preparation and technique.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Seat the patient quietly for at least 5 minutes; support back and arm with feet on the floor; use a calibrated device and correct cuff; measure both arms; average three readings 1-2 minutes apart. Repeat if readings differ by more than 10 mmHg.
ruleIn.normalValue: 120/80 mmHg is the Saudi guideline's normal reference value.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Confirm an elevated office result or assess suspected white-coat or masked hypertension.
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Average home blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg or higher for diagnosis; 135/85 mmHg or higher is the separate threshold at which treatment is considered.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Use a validated automatic monitor after at least 5 minutes seated in a quiet setting with back, legs and arm supported. Record two to three readings morning and evening for several days.
ruleIn.normalValue: Average home blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg under the Saudi diagnostic definition.

references.title: National Heart Center/Saudi Heart Association 2023 Guidelines on the Management of Hypertension

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Confirm office readings and identify white-coat, masked or isolated nocturnal hypertension.
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Twenty-four-hour average above 125/75 mmHg or night-time average above 110/65 mmHg meets the Saudi diagnostic definition.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Interpret daytime, night-time and 24-hour averages separately because their thresholds differ.
ruleIn.normalValue: Twenty-four-hour average 125/75 mmHg or lower and night-time average 110/65 mmHg or lower under the Saudi diagnostic definition.

references.title: National Heart Center/Saudi Heart Association 2023 Guidelines on the Management of Hypertension

ruleIn.modalityTarget: After suspected or confirmed hypertension: glucose or HbA1c, full blood count, lipid profile, creatinine with estimated glomerular filtration rate, sodium, potassium, calcium, thyroid-stimulating hormone and urinalysis.
ruleIn.targetCondition: Hypertension-mediated organ damage, cardiovascular risk or secondary hypertension
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Renal impairment, electrolyte disturbance, dysglycaemia, dyslipidaemia, thyroid abnormality, haematuria or proteinuria may change risk assessment or trigger targeted evaluation.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Interpret each result against the reporting laboratory's adult interval. Add urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio for diabetes, long-standing hypertension or established organ damage; it may also be used in suspected hypertension.
ruleIn.normalValue: Within the reporting laboratory's adult reference interval; the Saudi guideline does not set a single numeric normal range for this panel.

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Baseline evaluation after suspected or confirmed hypertension.
ruleIn.targetCondition: Cardiac target-organ damage or coexisting cardiac disease
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Left-ventricular hypertrophy, rhythm abnormality or evidence of cardiac disease may alter risk and prompt echocardiography or specialist review.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: A normal tracing does not exclude hypertension. Consider echocardiography when the electrocardiogram is abnormal or left-ventricular dysfunction or coronary disease is strongly suspected.
ruleIn.normalValue: No electrocardiographic evidence of hypertensive cardiac damage; interpret against the clinical context.

ruleOut.testName: Repeat office measurement after correct preparation
ruleOut.modalityTarget: An isolated elevated reading or inconsistent readings.
ruleOut.expectedFinding: The average falls below the Saudi office diagnostic threshold after standardised repeat measurement.
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Do not label sustained hypertension from a poorly performed or isolated reading. Use the higher arm for subsequent readings when arms differ.
ruleOut.normalValue: Below 130/80 mmHg under the Saudi office diagnostic definition.

references.title: National Heart Center/Saudi Heart Association 2023 Guidelines on the Management of Hypertension

ruleOut.modalityTarget: First assessment; especially older adults, people with diabetes, symptoms or conditions associated with orthostatic hypotension.
ruleOut.targetCondition: Orthostatic hypotension affecting interpretation or treatment safety
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Symptoms or a fall after standing indicates that management should account for postural blood pressure.
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Measure after 1 minute and 3 minutes standing from a seated position. The opened Saudi source specifies timing but does not state a numeric diagnostic fall in this section.
ruleOut.normalValue: No symptomatic postural fall; no numeric normal threshold is asserted from the opened source.

clinicalManagement.title: Screen with standardised office measurement
clinicalManagement.timeframe: At each healthcare visit when feasible
actions: Screen all adults older than 18 years. Screen annually after age 40 or when hypertension risk factors are present; otherwise screen every 3-5 years (NHC/SHA 2023, section 3.3.1, Table 4).
Seat quietly for at least 5 minutes; support the back and arm; keep both feet on the floor; use a calibrated validated device and correct cuff (section 3.2.1, Figure 1).
Measure both arms. Average three readings taken 1-2 minutes apart; take additional measurements when readings differ by more than 10 mmHg (section 3.2.1).

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm persistence outside the office
actions: Use validated home or 24-hour ambulatory monitoring to confirm office readings and detect white-coat, masked or nocturnal hypertension (NHC/SHA 2023, section 3.2.2, Tables 2-3).
Keep diagnostic thresholds separate from treatment-consideration thresholds. Record the method, time period and average used.
If repeat office and out-of-office results disagree, document the phenotype rather than averaging readings from different methods.

branches.condition: Office elevated; home or ambulatory average below its diagnostic threshold
actions: Document possible white-coat hypertension and continue risk-based surveillance.

branches.condition: Office below threshold; home or ambulatory average elevated
actions: Document possible masked hypertension and complete cardiovascular and organ-damage assessment.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess risk, organ damage and secondary causes
clinicalManagement.timeframe: At confirmation or while confirmation is arranged
actions: Record previous readings, family history, cardiovascular and renal disease, medicines and substances, exercise, weight change, diet, smoking, sleep and pregnancy possibility (NHC/SHA 2023, section 3.4, Table 6).
Perform the baseline laboratory panel, urinalysis and electrocardiogram. Add targeted testing only when history, examination or baseline results suggest a secondary cause.
Consider echocardiography when the electrocardiogram is abnormal or left-ventricular dysfunction or coronary disease is strongly suspected.

clinicalManagement.title: Escalate suspected hypertensive emergency
actions: Use an emergency pathway when blood pressure is above 190/120 mmHg with new or worsening hypertension-mediated organ damage (NHC/SHA 2023, Table 20).
Send severe elevation with chest pain, dyspnoea, acute neurological deficit, confusion or visual loss for urgent hospital assessment.
Use a pregnancy-specific pathway for any pregnant patient with elevated blood pressure.

clinicalManagement.title: Document and arrange follow-up
actions: Record the measurement method, arm, cuff, readings, average, symptoms, organ-damage assessment and confirmation plan.
After treatment begins or while blood pressure remains uncontrolled, review in 1-2 months; once controlled, review every 3-6 months (NHC/SHA 2023, section 3.3.2, Table 5).
Give lifestyle advice and clear instructions for urgent symptoms; treatment choice belongs in the full hypertension-management pathway.

medicationPlan.note: This topic covers screening and confirmation. It does not prescribe medicines. Use the governed hypertension-treatment pathway after diagnosis and risk assessment.

teaching.scope: Adult hypertension screening and confirmation in Saudi primary care.
learningObjectives: Perform a standardised office blood-pressure assessment and select the correct out-of-office confirmation method.
Keep Saudi diagnostic thresholds separate from treatment-consideration thresholds.
Recognise organ-damage features that require immediate escalation.
pitfalls: Diagnosing sustained hypertension from one poorly performed office reading.
Combining office, home and ambulatory thresholds as if they were interchangeable.
Missing masked hypertension because the office reading is below threshold.
Delaying emergency assessment when severe elevation accompanies new organ damage.
keyPoints: Standardise technique before interpreting the number.
Use home or ambulatory averages to confirm and phenotype hypertension.
Assess cardiovascular risk, target-organ damage and secondary causes after suspected hypertension.

patientEducation: Hypertension is often symptom-free; follow-up depends on measured averages, not symptoms.
Show how to sit, position the arm and use a validated home monitor before relying on home readings.
Seek urgent care for chest pain, severe breathlessness, new neurological deficit, confusion or visual loss with a severe reading.
lifestyleAndDiet: Offer regular physical activity, weight management, smoking cessation and a balanced eating pattern.
Saudi MOH public advice recommends reducing salt to less than 5 g per day; individualise advice for comorbidity and local diet.
mdtReferrals: Primary care or family medicine for confirmation and cardiovascular-risk review.
Emergency care for suspected acute target-organ injury.
Relevant specialist service when a secondary cause or established organ damage is suspected.
dischargeCriteria: No feature requiring immediate hospital assessment.
Measurement method and results are documented.
Home or ambulatory confirmation and follow-up responsibility are arranged.
The patient understands urgent symptoms and home-monitoring technique.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: The ordering primary-care clinician reviews the home or ambulatory average and baseline tests. Review in 1-2 months after treatment initiation or adjustment and every 3-6 months once controlled; use a shorter interval when organ damage, pregnancy or secondary hypertension is suspected.
